topicName: Serving Scikit-learn Pipelines with ONNX and MLflow
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Serving Scikit-learn Pipelines with ONNX and MLflow"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In production machine learning environments, high-performance inference and robust model tracking are critical requirements. This tutorial covers how to train a Scikit-learn pipeline, convert it to the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) format for optimized execution, and manage its lifecycle using MLflow."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have the necessary libraries installed. You will need scikit-learn, mlflow, onnx, skl2onnx, and onnxruntime."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install scikit-learn mlflow onnx skl2onnx onnxruntime"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Training a Scikit-learn Pipeline"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"We begin by creating a standard Scikit-learn pipeline consisting of a standard scaler for feature normalization and a random forest classifier for prediction."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

iris = load_iris()
X, y = iris.data, iris.target

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("classifier", RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=10, random_state=42))
])

pipeline.fit(X, y)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Converting the Pipeline to ONNX"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"To convert the Scikit-learn pipeline into the ONNX format, we use the skl2onnx library. We must define the initial input type matching the shape and data type of our input features."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from skl2onnx import convert_sklearn
from skl2onnx.common.data_types import FloatTensorType
import onnx

initial_type = [("float_input", FloatTensorType([None, 4]))]
onnx_model = convert_sklearn(pipeline, initial_types=initial_type)

onnx.save_model(onnx_model, "iris_pipeline.onnx")"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Tracking and Logging with MLflow"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"MLflow allows us to track experiments, log parameters, and store our ONNX model as an artifact for reproducible deployments."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import mlflow

mlflow.set_experiment("onnx-sklearn-pipeline")

with mlflow.start_run() as run:
    mlflow.log_param("model_type", "RandomForestClassifier")
    mlflow.log_artifact("iris_pipeline.onnx")
    print(f"Model logged successfully in run {run.info.run_id}")"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Serving the ONNX Model"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"With the model registered as an artifact, you can load the ONNX runtime session for high-performance inference without relying on Python-heavy Scikit-learn pickling mechanisms."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort

ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("iris_pipeline.onnx")

input_name = ort_session.get_inputs()[0].name
output_name = ort_session.get_outputs()[0].name

sample_data = np.array([[5.1, 3.5, 1.4, 0.2]], dtype=np.float32)
result = ort_session.run([output_name], {input_name: sample_data})

print("Predicted Class:", result[0])"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":19,"bullet_point":"Pipelines group preprocessing and modeling steps together securely."},{"order":20,"bullet_point":"skl2onnx bridges Scikit-learn and the cross-platform ONNX runtime."},{"order":21,"bullet_point":"MLflow ensures models are systematically tracked and ready for production deployment."}]
